references: libical CHANGELOG 4.0.8 (unreleased): DST-gap time drift in ICU builds
resolution.why: RFC 5545 §3.3.5 reads a wall time a change to summer time skips with the UTC offset from before the change. libical 4.0.7 places the skipped day's occurrence so (03:30 EDT), but in its ICU build the next day keeps the later time of day too (fixed in libical 4.0.8: 'recurrences with a DAILY or longer frequency no longer move to a later time of day after an occurrence or DTSTART falls in a DST gap'). ical.js reads the skipped wall time with the offset from after the change, an hour early, and is right on every other day. So every day follows ical.js except the skipped day, which follows libical.

cases.why: 02:30 does not exist on 2019-03-10 in New York (02:00 EST becomes 03:00 EDT): that occurrence is at 03:30 EDT, the UTC offset before the gap; the next day is 02:30 again.

references: libical CHANGELOG 4.0.8 (unreleased): DST-gap time drift in ICU builds
resolution.why: RFC 5545 §3.3.5 reads a wall time a change to summer time skips with the UTC offset from before the change. libical 4.0.7 places the skipped day's occurrence so (02:45 +11:00), but in its ICU build the next day keeps the later time of day too (fixed in libical 4.0.8: 'recurrences with a DAILY or longer frequency no longer move to a later time of day after an occurrence or DTSTART falls in a DST gap'). ical.js reads the skipped wall time with the offset from after the change, an hour early, and is right on every other day. So every day follows ical.js except the skipped day, which follows libical.

cases.why: A 30-minute change: Lord Howe goes from 02:00 (+10:30) to 02:30 (+11:00) on 2019-10-06, so 02:15 that day is 02:45.
